keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Observe your land for a full season before major earthworks
keyPoints.draft: Sedzani land yaṋu kha khalaṅwaha yoṱhe ni sa athu ita major earthworks

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Catch and store rain, sun, and biomass before they leave your property
keyPoints.draft: Farani nahone ni vhulunge mvula, ḓuvha na biomass zwi sa athu bva kha ndaka yaṋu

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Edges and margins can be useful places to observe what grows well
keyPoints.draft: Edges na margins zwi nga vha fhethu hu vhuedzaho ha u sedza zwine zwa aluwa zwavhuḓi

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Hail injury to maize depends on the storm and the crop’s growth stage
keyPoints.draft: Hail injury kha maize i ya nga storm na growth stage ya crop

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer wants to dig swales to harvest rainwater. What should she do first, following 'observe and interact'?
question.draft: Mulimi u ṱoḓa u bwa swales u itela u kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula. Ndi mini zwine a fanela u ranga u zwi ita a tshi tevhedza observe and interact?

options.sourceEnglish: Dig immediately after the first good rain
options.draft: Bwani nga u ṱavhanya nga murahu ha mvula ya u ranga yavhuḓi

options.sourceEnglish: Watch where water flows and pools across at least one wet season
options.draft: Sedzani hune maḓi a elela hone na hune a kuvhangana hone kha at least one wet season
Kopisani kuitele kwa swale ya muhura

options.sourceEnglish: Assume the same swale design fits every site
options.draft: Humbulani uri design nthihi ya swale i lingana na site iṅwe na iṅwe

rationale.sourceEnglish: A wet season shows more than one storm, but observation is only a first step. Check the soil, slope, drainage and safe overflow route with a trained local adviser before digging.
rationale.draft: Khalaṅwaha ya mvula i sumbedza madumbu a no fhira ḽithihi, fhedzi u sedza ndi vhukando ha u ranga fhedzi. Musi ni sa athu bwa, na mueletshedzi wa henefho o gudedzwaho, tolani mavu, slope, drainage na safe overflow route.

question.sourceEnglish: Which layout best applies 'integrate rather than segregate'?
question.draft: Ndi layout ifhio ine ya shumisa zwavhuḓi integrate rather than segregate?

options.sourceEnglish: Chickens penned far from the garden
options.draft: Khuhu dzo valelwaho kule na tsimu

options.sourceEnglish: Garden, fruit trees and a chicken run arranged so chickens use an empty bed after harvest, then the farmer checks safe management before edible crops return
options.draft: Tsimu, miri ya mitshelo na chicken run zwo vhekanywa nga nḓila ine khuhu dza shumisa planting bed i si na zwimela nga murahu ha harvest; nga murahu mulimi u tola safe management musi edible crops dzi sa athu vhuya
Paddocks dzo fhambanaho dza crop iṅwe na iṅwe

options.sourceEnglish: All animals kept off the cultivated zone
options.draft: Zwifuwo zwoṱhe zwi dzule nnḓa ha cultivated zone

rationale.sourceEnglish: Integration puts each element to work for its neighbours — here, chickens clean up pests and add fertility instead of sitting idle in a fixed pen. Fresh manure can carry germs, so check safe management before edible crops return.
rationale.draft: Integration i ita uri element iṅwe na iṅwe i shumele zwine zwa vha tsini nayo — hafha, khuhu dzi clean up pests na u engedza fertility, nṱhani ha u dzula dzi sa shumi kha fixed pen. Fresh manure i nga hwalela germs, ngauralo tola safe management musi edible crops dzi sa athu vhuya.

review: Independent semantic backcheck accepted the wet-season/pooling observation, trained local adviser before digging, post-harvest safety check before edible crops return, and manure/germ condition. Unreviewed machine draft; not fluent-speaker or local-farming approval.
